gap: No result ChatGPT got states that SoundStage's Thom Moon measured the Fluance RT81+ at 33.5 rpm (about 0.55% fast) with ±0.17% wow at 33⅓, and 45.16 rpm (0.36% fast) with ±0.21% wow at 45, against Fluance's 0.2% wow-and-flutter claim.
standout_why: I compared against valveandvinyl.com (crosley-alternatives), platterandplinth.com (best-with-preamp) and fewbetter.com. Valve & Vinyl says every figure it gives is the maker's, with no named reviewer or lab. Platter & Plinth uses maker and listing figures only and says it does not run a lab. fewbetter's page has no turntable data at all. vinylpickup.com failed to load (bad SSL certificate), so I couldn't check it. None of the readable pages has a single measured speed or wow figure for any candidate. The finding is new, but it is one model measured with a phone app, not a test record or a lab.
decides: This confirms the pick rather than changing it. The RT81+ runs slightly fast by Moon's app reading, and its wow at 45 rpm (±0.21%) is a little over Fluance's 0.2% claim, but Moon says he heard no effect on the music. No named reviewer has published speed or wow-and-flutter figures for the AT-LP70X, AT-LP70XBT, Sony PS-LX3BT or AT-LP120XUSB, so there is no measured head-to-head that could move the pick away from ChatGPT's AT-LP70X-or-Fluance answer. The page can say honestly that the RT81+ is the only candidate with published measured speed figures.

findings.label: Measured speed at 33⅓ rpm
findings.source_title: SoundStage! Access: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge (Thom Moon)
findings.note: Thom Moon used 'the RPM app on my phone', not a test record or lab rig. Page created 15 February 2024. (33.5 − 33.333) / 33.333 = 0.5%; Moon writes 'about 0.55%'.

findings.label: Measured wow at 33⅓ rpm
findings.source_title: SoundStage! Access: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge (Thom Moon)
findings.note: Phone-app estimate, which Moon calls 'estimated wow'. He gives no flutter figure. Fluance claims 0.2% wow and flutter.

findings.label: Measured speed and wow at 45 rpm
findings.source_title: SoundStage! Access: Fluance RT81+ Turntable and Audio-Technica AT-VM95E Cartridge (Thom Moon)
findings.note: Same phone app. Moon says the speed results were above Fluance's claims but that this 'didn't seem to affect the music'. The review gives the price as $299.99 (February 2024); that is not a current price.

findings.label: Measured tracking force (out of the box)
findings.note: hifi.de writes 'Bei unserem Sony PS-LX3BT messen wir 3,7 Gramm' (on our sample we measure 3.7 g) and says this is still within the recommended range. Platter & Plinth quotes Sony's spec as 3.5 ± 0.5 g. hifi.de gives no speed or wow figures, only that the pitch is stable.

findings.label: Tracking force on the review sample
findings.source_title: hifi.de: Audio-Technica AT-LP70XBT im Test (Bernhard Rietschel, 27 June 2025)
findings.note: Rietschel writes that it is right 'to the tenth' on the test unit ('stimmt beim Testgerät aufs Zehntel genau'), which implies a check on the sample, though the text doesn't explicitly call it a measurement. He says the deck runs fairly speed-stable but gives no speed or wow number.

findings.label: TechGearLab scores (Max Mutter, December 2017)
findings.value: RT81: 74 overall, 7.0 sound, 8.0 vibration resistance. AT-LP120XUSB: 81 overall, 8.0 sound, 6.0 vibration resistance
findings.note: These are scores, not instrument measurements. Vibration resistance was tested by bumping the table until the record skipped. The AT-LP120XUSB scores are from https://techgearlab.com/reviews/audio/turntable/audio-technica-at-lp120xusb, read the same day. Both tests date from 2017.

unsourced: Measured speed or wow and flutter for the AT-LP70X and AT-LP70XBT. I searched in English and German (Messwerte, Gleichlauf) and read the hifi.de AT-LP70XBT test. Digital Trends, TechRadar and Louder appear in searches, but no excerpt I saw had numbers.
Measured speed or wow and flutter for the Sony PS-LX3BT and PS-LX310BT. hifi.de reports only tracking force. Searches turned up only Sony's 0.1% spec and user anecdotes.

Newport Test Labs measurements of the AT-LP120XUSB (Steve Holding's 2020 'Laboratory Test Report'). The search excerpt says platter speed was 'exact' and rotational stability 'excellent', but both Everand article URLs returned 404, so I have no number.
AnalogPlanet's RT81+ review (analogplanet.com/node/125325) returned 403, so I couldn't check it for figures.
The RT81+ spec and price on fluance.com: the product URL returned 404, and storecheck.py search on fluance.com returned HTTP 404.
Measured preamp output level or noise for any candidate. No named reviewer published one in anything I opened.
